operations.before: A stubborn, dark algae that grows in tufts on plants, decorations, and equipment. Often indicates fluctuating CO₂ levels. Removed by spot-treating with hydrogen peroxide.
operations.after: A stubborn, dark algae that grows in tufts on plants, decorations and equipment. It is associated with fluctuating CO₂, plant stress and organic buildup. Correct the husbandry cause first; any chemical treatment requires a livestock-safety review and specialist guidance.

operations.before: Do not pour warm water straight into the tank | Do not raise temperature more than 1–2 °C per day during treatment
operations.after: Do not pour warm water straight into the tank | Do not make abrupt temperature changes; restore stable conditions gradually and seek species-specific guidance.

operations.before: Abdomen swells and scales stand out like a pinecone — usually a bacterial infection.
operations.after: A swollen abdomen with scales standing out like a pinecone is a sign of fluid imbalance, not a single disease. Cause and treatment depend on the species and diagnosis; seek aquatic-veterinary advice.

operations.before: Unstable CO₂, irregular fertilisation and ammonia/organic spikes are associated with plant stress
operations.after: Associated factors, not confirmed causes: unstable CO₂, irregular fertilisation and ammonia/organic spikes with plant stress.

operations.before: The most popular freshwater shrimp — bright red coloration, extremely hardy, and prolific breeder. The gateway species for shrimp keeping. Tolerates a wide range of conditions.
operations.after: Trade-name form of Neocaridina davidi, the same species as Red Cherry Shrimp. Kept for trade-name search continuity; species-level care applies. Not a separate species.
